thread:
marta: quick sync 4GRPC streaming for internal inference proxy: pros/cons? thinking about migrating our front proxy from JSON SSE -> grpc-web. main goals: accurate per-request quota, fewer proxy-induced retries, better multiplexing for long-lived sessions.

devin: big +1 for fewer retries. our current setup sometimes double-counts tokens when a proxy retries a streaming call.

marta: exactly. we see billing blips when edge retries cause the runtime to re-ingest prompts. hard to tell in console which side re-sent.

theo: downside: browsers need grpc-web shims and some of our legacy customers rely on plain SSE. Also gateway observability for grpc streams is less mature; we lose easy per-chunk metrics.

lina: for telemetry we need a strategy: if we move to gRPC streaming, payload-level token reporting must still be runtime-sourced. gateway should only emit transport metrics. then console join logic matches runtime.token_reports with gateway.transport_events by trace_id.

gabe: on quotas: we can switch to a "lease" model over the stream: client requests a token lease for N tokens at start of stream; runtime charges against the lease incrementally. avoids double-charge on reconnects. but complexity increases.

marta: lease model sounds promising for long sessions (e.g., interactive chat). but short-lived bursts (single request-response) don't need it. maybe hybrid: lease for streams > 1s or > X tokens.

devin: how do we handle middleboxes that terminate/replace trace headers? We rely on x-rw-trace. If a proxy reconnects a stream, trace changes and joins fail. We should enforce trace-propagation tests in e2e smoke.

infra-bot: TASK INF-701 created: add trace-propagation checks for grpc-web proxies. Assigned to @theo.

lina: console UX asks: we should surface "stream state" in the per-call row: (open|closed|reconnected) and show attribution (runtime|gateway|inferred). otherwise SREs will run to pager.

marta: rollout plan idea: 1) introduce grpc-web endpoint alongside SSE (flagged), 2) instrument logical_stream_id + initial_lease header, 3) collect telemetry for 2 weeks, 4) flip clients after canary.

theo: canary idea: start with internal infra traffic (10k reqs/min) then 5% customer traffic. Also add a metric: reconnection_rate per logical_stream_id. alert if >0.2% sustained.

gabe: one more gotcha: protobuf packing vs json text affects gateway compression and chunking. grpc binary will reduce chunk count, which helps telemetry but may mask subtle token differences. runtime must still be sole source for tokens.

devin: agree. make a hard rule: billing uses runtime.token_report if present; otherwise fallback to gateway.bytes_estimate. the console should show which was used.

lina: implement a dedupe window: if gateway and runtime reports have same logical_stream_id within 60s, prefer runtime. if mismatch, mark item "needs-investigation" in UI.

marta: security note: grpc-web auth token expiry flows are slightly different. need to ensure refresh path for long-lived streams doesn't silently drop. add to rollout checklist.

infra-bot: NOTE: added grpc-web auth refresh test to INF-701.

theo: implementation tasks I'll create: gateway: accept grpc-web, emit logical_stream_id & initial_lease metric; runtime: accept lease header and emit periodic token deltas; console: attribution column + reconnection_rate chart.

gabe: please use histogram buckets for stream sizes, don't create per-stream gauges. cardinality pls.

devin: small code snippet for initial_lease header idea:

```
:authority: api.redwood.ai
x-rw-logical-stream-id: s-12345
x-rw-initial-lease: 1024
```

marta: thanks. can we add a brief blurb in docs explaining why customers might see small differences when switching protocols (SSE -> gRPC) and how to interpret console attribution? helps reduce support noise.

lina: will draft a short doc and console banner copy.

marta: ok closing notes 5we'll track INF-701, run a 2-week telemetry collection, and prepare a 5% canary. I'll follow up with a rollout doc and a timeline. thanks all :thumbsup:
